The promotion of political isolationism among member states.
The reduction of trade barriers among member states.
The creation of a unified military force for external defense.

questions.explanation: One of the primary objectives of ECOWAS is to promote economic integration among West African states. A key aspect of this objective is the reduction of trade barriers, facilitating freer movement of goods and services among member states.

questions.question_text: A major distinction between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria relates to the structure of the executive. Which of the following best describes this difference?

options.text: The 1979 Constitution established a parliamentary system, while the 1999 Constitution established a presidential system
The 1979 Constitution had a presidential system, while the 1999 Constitution introduced a semi-parliamentary system
The 1979 Constitution adopted a presidential system, whereas the 1999 Constitution retained the same system with minor adjustments
The 1979 Constitution had a unicameral legislature, while the 1999 Constitution introduced a bicameral legislature

questions.explanation: Both the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria adopted a presidential system of government. The main difference lies in certain adjustments and provisions made in the 1999 Constitution. Therefore, option C is correct as it accurately reflects that both constitutions maintained a presidential system.

The authority of the judiciary to unilaterally make laws
The power of the executive to dissolve the legislature at will

options.text: The state is subject to external control
The state has the ultimate power to make decisions within its borders
The state's authority is limited by international law
The state's power is divided among various institutions

questions.explanation: Sovereignty means that a state has the ultimate power to govern itself and make decisions within its territory without external interference. Thus, option B accurately describes the implication of sovereignty.

questions.question_text: A major distinction between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria relates to the structure of the executive. Which of the following best describes this difference?

options.text: The 1979 Constitution established a parliamentary system, while the 1999 Constitution established a presidential system
The 1979 Constitution adopted a presidential system, while the 1999 Constitution adopted a semi-presidential system
The 1979 Constitution had a single four-year term for the president, while the 1999 Constitution allows for multiple four-year terms
The 1979 Constitution established a presidential system with a single term limit, while the 1999 Constitution maintained the presidential system but removed the single term limit

questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution of Nigeria established a presidential system with a single four-year term for the president. In contrast, the 1999 Constitution maintained the presidential system but allowed for multiple four-year terms. Thus, the correct description of the difference is that the 1979 Constitution had a single term limit, while the 1999 Constitution removed this limit.

The legislative arm can impeach the president and other executive officials
The judiciary has the power to make laws without input from the other arms
The executive has absolute power to dissolve the legislature

The power to make decisions without external interference
The requirement to follow international law in all domestic matters
The necessity of having a monarch as the head of state

questions.explanation: Sovereignty is characterized by a state's ability to exercise supreme authority within its territory without external interference. This means that a sovereign state has the power to make decisions regarding its internal and external affairs independently.

questions.question_text: In a parliamentary system of government, the head of state is usually responsible for appointing the head of government, who is typically the leader of the majority party or coalition in the legislature. options.text: Separation of powers between the legislative, executive, and judiciary
The head of state and head of government are the same person
The head of government is accountable to the legislature

questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the head of government is accountable to the legislature, meaning they must maintain the confidence of the legislature to remain in office. This is a fundamental characteristic that distinguishes parliamentary systems from presidential systems.

To monitor and review revenue allocation formulae
To determine the fiscal policy of the government

questions.explanation: The Revenue Mobilization Allocation and Fiscal Commission is responsible for monitoring and reviewing revenue allocation formulae among the three tiers of government in Nigeria, ensuring that the allocation is fair and in line with the constitution.

questions.topic: Arms of Government and Electoral Processes
questions.question_text: In a parliamentary system of government, the head of state is usually responsible for appointing the head of government, who is typically the leader of the majority party or coalition in the legislature. Which of the following is a characteristic of this system?

options.text: The head of state and head of government are the same person
The head of government is responsible to the legislature
The executive is not accountable to the legislature

questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the head of government is typically the prime minister, who is responsible to the legislature. This means they must maintain the confidence of the legislature to remain in office. The correct answer, B, reflects this characteristic. Option A is incorrect because, in a parliamentary system, the head of state and head of government are usually different individuals. Option C is incorrect because the judiciary is expected to be independent in a parliamentary system. Option D is incorrect because, in a parliamentary system, the executive (headed by the prime minister) is indeed accountable to the legislature.

questions.question_text: The 1999 Constitution of Nigeria provides for the establishment of a Revenue Mobilization Allocation and Fiscal Commission. What is the primary function of this commission?

options.text: To monitor and ensure the proper allocation of revenue among the tiers of government
To oversee the country's foreign policy
To manage the country's defense budget
To regulate the activities of political parties

questions.explanation: The Revenue Mobilization Allocation and Fiscal Commission is established to monitor and ensure the proper allocation of revenue among the different tiers of government in Nigeria. This includes reviewing the revenue allocation formula and ensuring compliance with it. Option A accurately describes this primary function. Options B, C, and D are incorrect as they describe functions unrelated to the commission's role.

questions.explanation: The diagram represents a system where a single ruler has absolute power with no checks on their authority. This is characteristic of an autocracy, where one person holds complete control over the government. Option B, Autocracy, is the correct answer. Option A, Democracy, is incorrect because it involves rule by the people, either directly or through elected representatives. Option C, Oligarchy, is incorrect because it refers to rule by a small group of people, not necessarily one individual. Option D, Theocracy, is incorrect because it refers to a system where religious leaders hold power, which is not specified in the diagram.

questions.topic: Nigeria's Foreign Policy and International Relations
questions.question_text: One of the primary objectives of Nigeria's participation in the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is to promote economic integration among member states. Which of the following is a key strategy for achieving this objective?

options.text: Promoting bilateral trade agreements with non-member states
Encouraging the free movement of persons and goods
Imposing trade barriers on non-member states

questions.explanation: ECOWAS aims to promote economic integration among its member states. One key strategy for achieving this is by encouraging the free movement of persons and goods, which facilitates trade and economic cooperation. Option C accurately describes this strategy. Option A, while related, is not the primary strategy as ECOWAS has faced challenges in implementing a common currency. Option B is incorrect because promoting bilateral trade agreements with non-member states is not a primary strategy for achieving economic integration among member states. Option D is incorrect because imposing trade barriers on non-member states is protectionist and not a strategy for integration among member states.

questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of sovereignty?

options.text: The ability to impose taxes without consent
The power to make laws without external influence
The authority to enforce laws within its territory

questions.explanation: Sovereignty refers to the supreme authority of a state within its territory. This includes the ability to impose taxes without external consent (A), the power to make laws without external influence (B), and the authority to enforce laws within its territory (C). All these characteristics are aspects of sovereignty, making Option D the correct answer. Each of the individual options (A, B, C) describes a facet of sovereignty, and together they comprehensively define it.

questions.question_text: A major distinction between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria relates to the structure of the executive. options.text: The 1999 Constitution concentrated more power in the hands of the President
The 1979 Constitution concentrated more power in the hands of the President
The 1999 Constitution provided for a weaker executive
The 1979 Constitution provided for a parliamentary system

questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, like the 1979 Constitution, adopts a Presidential system. However, the 1999 Constitution is noted for concentrating significant powers in the office of the President, making the President both the head of state and head of government. options.text: The President vetoing a bill passed by the National Assembly
The National Assembly approving the President's ministerial appointments
The National Assembly impeaching the President
The President appointing Supreme Court Justices

questions.explanation: The principle of checks and balances is fundamental to the separation of powers in Nigeria's federal system. One way the legislative arm checks the executive is through the power of impeachment. The National Assembly has the constitutional power to impeach the President under certain circumstances, such as gross misconduct. This serves as a significant check on the executive arm, ensuring that the President does not abuse his powers.

The creation of a unified passport for member states

The abolition of visa requirements among member states

questions.question_text: In Nigeria's federal system, the principle of checks and balances is designed to prevent any one arm of government from becoming too powerful. Which of the following is an example of this principle in action?

options.text: The power of the President to appoint ministers without Senate approval
The ability of the National Assembly to impeach the President
The power of the judiciary to declare laws passed by the legislature as unconstitutional
The legislature's ability to amend the constitution without executive approval

questions.explanation: The principle of checks and balances is exemplified when one arm of government can restrain the actions of another. The judiciary's power to declare laws passed by the legislature as unconstitutional is a classic example of this principle. Options A and D are incorrect because they describe actions that either violate the principle of checks and balances or are not accurate representations of the Nigerian system. Option B, while correct in principle, is not the best example among those listed.

questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of a sovereign state?

options.text: The ability to make laws without external influence
The presence of a monarch as head of state

questions.explanation: A sovereign state is characterized by its ability to exercise supreme authority within its territory, free from external control. This means it can make laws and decisions without external influence, making option A the correct answer. Options B, C, and D are incorrect because they do not necessarily define a sovereign state; a sovereign state can have various forms of government (not just a monarchy), can choose to be part of international organizations, and can have different systems of government (not limited to federal).

Promoting bilateral trade agreements with non-ECOWAS countries
Encouraging the free movement of persons and goods
Imposing uniform tariffs on imports from non-member states

questions.explanation: One of the key strategies for achieving economic integration among ECOWAS member states is encouraging the free movement of persons and goods. The state's power is derived from external sources

The capacity to enter into international agreements

questions.explanation: Nigeria's participation in ECOWAS aims to promote economic integration among member states. Key aspects of this objective include establishing a common currency (the Eco), creating a unified economic policy, and promoting cultural exchange programs. While a unified military force (ECOWAS Standby Force) is also a feature, the primary focus is on economic integration, making 'All of the above' a correct representation of the broad objectives, though with varying degrees of implementation.

questions.topic: Arms of Government and Electoral Processes
questions.question_text: In Nigeria's federal system, the principle of checks and balances is designed to prevent any one arm of government from becoming too powerful. Which of the following is an example of this principle in action?

options.text: The power of the President to appoint ministers without Senate approval
The ability of the National Assembly to impeach the President
The authority of the Executive to make laws without legislative input
The independence of the Judiciary to interpret laws without executive oversight

questions.explanation: The principle of checks and balances is fundamental in ensuring that no single arm of government dominates the others. The ability of the National Assembly to impeach the President is a direct application of this principle, as it allows the Legislative to hold the Executive accountable. Option B is correct because impeachment is a constitutional power vested in the Legislature to check the Executive. Options A and C are incorrect because they suggest unchecked power, contrary to the principle of checks and balances. Option D, while true in stating the independence of the Judiciary, does not directly illustrate the principle of checks and balances between the arms of government.

questions.question_text: A significant distinction between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria is related to the structure of the executive. Which of the following accurately describes this difference?

options.text: The 1979 Constitution established a parliamentary system, while the 1999 Constitution established a presidential system
The 1979 Constitution provided for a single-term presidency, while the 1999 Constitution allowed for multiple terms
The 1979 Constitution adopted a presidential system with a weak executive, while the 1999 Constitution strengthened the executive
The 1979 Constitution had a presidential system with limited executive powers, while the 1999 Constitution expanded these powers

questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution of Nigeria adopted a presidential system of government but with certain limitations on the executive powers. The 1999 Constitution, on the other hand, maintained the presidential system but with significant enhancements to the powers of the executive, particularly the President. Thus, option C accurately captures the distinction between the two constitutions regarding the structure and powers of the executive. Options A, B, and D are incorrect as they either misrepresent the system of government adopted by the constitutions or inaccurately describe the changes in executive powers.

Promoting a single political system across member states
Implementing a unified defense policy for the region
Reducing trade barriers among member states

questions.explanation: ECOWAS aims to promote economic integration among its member states through various strategies. One key strategy is reducing trade barriers, which facilitates the free movement of goods and services across borders. Option D is correct as it accurately describes a fundamental approach used by ECOWAS to achieve economic integration. Option A, while related, is not entirely accurate as ECOWAS has explored a common currency (Eco) but it's not yet implemented for all members. Options B and C are incorrect because they refer to political and defense unification, which are not primary economic integration strategies.

questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of a sovereign state?

options.text: The ability to make laws without external influence
The power to enforce laws only within its borders
The capacity to enter into international treaties

questions.explanation: Sovereignty refers to the supreme authority of a state within its territory. A sovereign state has the ability to make laws without external influence (A), the power to enforce laws within its borders (B), and the capacity to engage in international relations, including entering into treaties (C). All these characteristics are attributes of a sovereign state. Therefore, option D, 'All of the above,' is the correct answer as it encompasses the various aspects of sovereignty.

It introduced a diarchical executive system

Therefore, the correct answer is that it maintained the same executive structure as the 1979 Constitution.

It is limited by international law
It is subject to the will of the people

To reduce the role of the legislature

questions.question_text: A major difference between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria is related to the \( \text{structure of the executive} \). The 1999 Constitution is characterized by

options.text: a presidential system with a weak executive
a strong presidential system with enhanced executive powers

questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution of Nigeria is characterized by a strong presidential system where the President has significant executive powers, unlike the 1979 Constitution which had some differences in the distribution of executive powers. The correct answer, 'a strong presidential system with enhanced executive powers,' reflects this characteristic. Option A is incorrect because Nigeria has never adopted a parliamentary system. Option B is incorrect as the 1999 Constitution actually strengthened the executive. Option D is incorrect as Nigeria is not a constitutional monarchy.

questions.topic: Arms of Government and Electoral Processes
questions.question_text: In Nigeria's federal system, the principle of separation of powers is crucial because it

options.text: ensures that the executive has absolute power
allows the legislature to override the judiciary
prevents any one arm of government from becoming too powerful
eliminates the need for checks and balances

questions.explanation: The principle of separation of powers is crucial in Nigeria's federal system because it ensures that power is distributed among the three arms of government: the legislative, executive, and judiciary. This distribution prevents any one arm from becoming too powerful, thus safeguarding against authoritarianism. Option C correctly captures this principle. Option A is incorrect because separation of powers limits, rather than concentrates, executive power. Option B is incorrect as it misrepresents the relationship between the legislature and judiciary. Option D is incorrect because checks and balances are complementary to the separation of powers.

dominate the economies of other West African countries
isolate itself from other West African countries
impose its political system on other member states

questions.explanation: Nigeria's participation in ECOWAS is primarily aimed at promoting economic integration among West African states. This includes enhancing trade, cooperation, and economic development within the region. Option A correctly states this objective. Option B is incorrect because ECOWAS aims for cooperation, not domination. Option C is incorrect as ECOWAS promotes integration, not isolation. Option D is incorrect because ECOWAS focuses on economic integration, not imposing political systems.

questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of sovereignty?

options.text: Authority restricted by international law only

questions.explanation: Sovereignty is characterized by a state's supreme authority within its territory, meaning it has the ultimate power to govern itself without external interference. Option B correctly describes this characteristic. Option A is incorrect because sovereignty implies supreme, not limited, authority. Option C is incorrect as sovereignty is not about sharing authority. Option D is incorrect because while international law may influence a state's actions, sovereignty is about the state's internal supreme authority.

questions.question_text: A major difference between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria is related to the structure of the executive. The 1979 Constitution adopted a \[ \text{parliamentary system} \], while the 1999 Constitution adopted a \[ \text{presidential system} \]. Which of the following is a characteristic of the executive structure under the 1999 Constitution?

options.text: The President is not directly elected by the people
The President is both the head of state and head of government
The executive power is vested in the Prime Minister
The President is responsible to the legislature

questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution of Nigeria adopted a presidential system where the President serves as both the head of state and head of government. This is a key characteristic of the executive structure under this constitution. Option B is correct because it accurately describes this characteristic. Options A, C, and D are incorrect because they either misrepresent the method of electing the President, misplace the vesting of executive power, or inaccurately describe the President's responsibility to the legislature under the 1999 Constitution.

questions.topic: Nigeria's Foreign Policy and International Relations
questions.question_text: One of the primary objectives of Nigeria's participation in the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is to promote economic integration among member states. Which of the following is a key strategy used by ECOWAS to achieve this objective?

options.text: Imposing tariffs on imports from non-member states
Establishing a common currency for member states
Promoting bilateral trade agreements between member states
Encouraging the free movement of persons and goods

questions.explanation: ECOWAS aims to promote economic integration among its member states through various strategies. One key strategy is encouraging the free movement of persons and goods, which facilitates trade and economic cooperation. Option D is correct as it accurately describes this strategy. Options A, B, and C are incorrect because while they may relate to economic policies, they do not accurately represent a primary strategy used by ECOWAS for promoting economic integration. ECOWAS has indeed worked towards a common currency (the Eco) but it's still in development, and while tariffs and bilateral agreements are relevant, the free movement is a cornerstone.

questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of sovereignty?

options.text: It is limited by international law
It is shared among different branches of government
It is derived from the people

questions.explanation: Sovereignty is characterized by being absolute and indivisible, meaning that the state's authority is supreme and not divided. Option B is correct because it accurately describes this characteristic. Options A, C, and D are incorrect because while sovereignty may be influenced by international law, it is not inherently limited by it; sovereignty is not shared among different branches of government as it refers to the state's overall authority; and while sovereignty may be derived from the people in democratic theory, this is not a defining characteristic of sovereignty itself.

questions.topic: Arms of Government and Electoral Processes
questions.question_text: In a parliamentary system of government, the head of state and head of government roles are typically held by different individuals. Which of the following is true about the head of government in a parliamentary system?

options.text: The head of government is directly elected by the people
The head of government is responsible to the legislature
The head of government has ceremonial duties only
The head of government is not accountable to the parliament

questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the head of government (usually called the Prime Minister) is responsible to the legislature. This means they must maintain the confidence of the legislature to remain in office. Option B is correct because it accurately describes this responsibility. Options A, C, and D are incorrect because the head of government is typically not directly elected by the people but is usually the leader of the majority party or coalition in the legislature; the head of government has significant executive powers beyond ceremonial duties; and the head of government is indeed accountable to the parliament.

questions.question_text: A major difference between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria is related to the structure of the executive. The 1979 Constitution had a \( \text{Diarchy} \) at the centre, while the 1999 Constitution has a \[ \text{single executive} \]. What does this imply?

options.text: The 1999 Constitution has a presidential system
The 1999 Constitution has a parliamentary system
The 1979 Constitution had a single executive

questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution had a Diarchy at the centre, meaning there was a dual executive structure involving both a President and a Prime Minister. In contrast, the 1999 Constitution has a single executive, meaning the President holds the primary executive powers. This implies that the 1999 Constitution has a presidential system where the President is both the head of state and head of government.

To promote economic integration and cooperation among member states

To create economic barriers among member states

This means that the state has the ultimate power to govern itself and make decisions without external interference. questions.question_text: A major difference between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria is related to the structure of the executive. The 1979 Constitution adopted a \[ \text{presidential system} \], while the 1999 Constitution \[ \text{retained} \] this system. Which of the following best describes the executive structure under both constitutions?
questions.explanation: Both the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria adopted a presidential system of government, where the President serves as both the head of state and head of government. This is in contrast to a parliamentary system where these roles are often separated. The presidential system is characterized by a clear separation of powers between the executive, legislative, and judicial branches. Therefore, the correct answer is B, as both constitutions retained the presidential system.

options.text: Concentration of power in the executive
Checks and balances among the arms of government

questions.explanation: The principle of separation of powers ensures that the legislative, executive, and judicial arms of government are independent and have distinct roles, thereby providing checks and balances among them. questions.question_text: A key distinction between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria relates to the structure of the executive. The 1979 Constitution established a \( \text{parliamentary system} \), while the 1999 Constitution adopted a \( \text{presidential system} \). What was the main implication of this change?

options.text: The reduction of the president's powers
The merging of legislative and executive functions
The concentration of executive power in the president
The abolition of the legislative arm

questions.explanation: The shift from a parliamentary system under the 1979 Constitution to a presidential system under the 1999 Constitution in Nigeria resulted in the concentration of executive power in the president. In a presidential system, the president serves as both the head of state and head of government, typically holding significant executive powers. Thus, option C is correct. Option A is incorrect because the change actually increased the president's powers. Option B is incorrect as the change did not merge the legislative and executive functions; rather, it maintained the separation of powers. Option D is incorrect because the legislative arm was not abolished.

The imposition of stricter tariffs on non-member states
The isolation of member states from global markets

questions.explanation: Promoting economic integration is a key objective of ECOWAS, and one of the direct benefits is the reduction of trade barriers among member states. Option B is incorrect because while tariffs might be adjusted, the primary focus is on reducing barriers among members, not necessarily imposing stricter tariffs on non-members. Option D is incorrect because while there are discussions about a single currency, the elimination of national currencies is not a direct benefit or current objective.

questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of a sovereign state?

options.text: The ability to make laws without external influence
The presence of a monarch as head of state
The existence of multiple political parties
The dependence on external authorities for defense

questions.explanation: Sovereignty refers to the supreme authority of a state within its territory, meaning it has the ultimate power to govern itself without external interference. A characteristic of a sovereign state is its ability to make laws and decisions independently. Thus, option A is correct. Option B is incorrect because sovereignty is not tied to the presence of a monarch; various forms of government can be sovereign. Option C is incorrect as the existence of multiple political parties is related to political pluralism, not directly to sovereignty. Option D is incorrect because dependence on external authorities contradicts the concept of sovereignty, which emphasizes independence and self-governance.

The state cannot make laws contrary to international norms.

To appoint key officials in the executive arm

questions.explanation: The judiciary plays a crucial role in a democratic system by interpreting the laws and ensuring their constitutionality. questions.topic: Arms of Government and Electoral Processes

The power to interpret the constitution

questions.explanation: In a democratic system, the legislative arm checks the executive arm through various mechanisms. One key example is the power to approve executive appointments. This ensures that the executive arm does not have unchecked authority in appointing officials. The legislative arm scrutinizes these appointments, thereby exercising oversight. Option B is correct because it accurately describes this check. Option A is incorrect because the power to grant pardons is typically an executive function. Option C is incorrect because interpreting the constitution is a judiciary role. Option D, while related to the executive, is not the best example of a legislative check on the executive as the power to declare war can be shared between the two arms depending on the constitution.

The 1979 and 1999 Constitutions had identical provisions on fundamental objectives and directive principles

questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution of Nigeria introduced the concept of fundamental objectives and directive principles of state policy. Option A is incorrect because the 1999 Constitution did not omit these principles. Option C is incorrect as both constitutions addressed both individual and collective rights. Checks and balances among the arms of government
Absolute authority of the executive arm

questions.explanation: The principle of separation of powers ensures that power is distributed among the legislative, executive, and judicial arms of government, preventing any one arm from becoming too powerful. This leads to checks and balances among the arms, as each arm has some ability to limit the actions of the other arms.

Absolute power vested in the President

Enhanced economic cooperation and free movement of goods and services

questions.explanation: ECOWAS aims to promote economic integration by reducing trade barriers and enhancing cooperation among member states. This leads to the free movement of goods, services, and people, ultimately boosting economic development in the region.

questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the head of government, typically called the Prime Minister, is responsible to the legislature. This means they must maintain the confidence of the legislature to remain in office. This characteristic is fundamental to the functioning of a parliamentary system, as it ensures accountability and checks the power of the executive.

questions.question_text: A key distinction between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria relates to the structure of the executive. The 1999 Constitution established a presidential system with a strong emphasis on which of the following?

options.text: Separation of powers between the executive and legislative branches
Concentration of power in the executive branch

It has the power to govern itself without external interference
It is governed by a monarch
It is a member of multiple international organizations

questions.explanation: Sovereignty refers to the supreme authority of a state within its territory. A sovereign state has the power to govern itself without external interference, making its own laws, policies, and decisions without being subject to the authority of another state or entity.

questions.question_text: A key distinction between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria relates to the structure of the executive. The 1999 Constitution established a presidential system with a strong executive president, while the 1979 Constitution had a more balanced approach between the executive and legislative arms. Which of the following best describes the implication of this distinction?

options.text: The 1999 Constitution concentrated more power in the hands of the president
The 1979 Constitution gave more power to the legislative arm
The 1999 Constitution reduced the role of the judiciary
The 1979 Constitution abolished the office of the president

questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution of Nigeria established a presidential system of government where the president serves as both the head of state and head of government, concentrating significant executive powers in the office of the president. This is in contrast to the 1979 Constitution, which, while also having a presidential system, had certain provisions that balanced power between the executive and legislative branches. Therefore, the correct answer is A, as it accurately describes the implication of the distinction between the two constitutions regarding the structure of the executive.

questions.topic: Arms of Government and Electoral Processes
questions.question_text: In a democratic system of government, the principle of checks and balances is designed to prevent the concentration of power in one arm of government. Which of the following is an example of the legislative arm checking the executive?

options.text: The legislature approving the president's nominees for ministerial appointments
The executive declaring a state of emergency without legislative approval
The judiciary interpreting laws passed by the legislature

questions.explanation: In a democratic system, the principle of checks and balances allows each arm of government to restrain the actions of the other arms. One way the legislative arm checks the executive is by approving or rejecting the president's nominees for ministerial appointments. This ensures that the executive does not have unchecked power in appointing officials. Therefore, option A is the correct example of the legislative arm checking the executive.

Imposing trade barriers to protect local industries

options.text: a two-thirds majority in the Senate and a simple majority in the House of Representatives
a two-thirds majority in both the Senate and the House of Representatives
a simple majority in both the Senate and the House of Representatives
a two-thirds majority in a joint session of the National Assembly

questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, similar to the 1979 Constitution, requires a two-thirds majority in both houses of the National Assembly for the impeachment of the president. The judiciary arm is responsible for making laws
The legislative arm is responsible for executing laws

impose its political system on other West African states

The power to enforce laws only within its borders
The authority to impose its will on other states
The capacity to be influenced by external forces

questions.explanation: Sovereignty refers to the supreme authority of a state within its territory, implying the ability to govern itself without external interference. Option A, 'The ability to make laws without external influence,' is a characteristic of sovereignty as it reflects the state's independence in law-making. Options B, C, and D are incorrect because while B is partially true, it doesn't fully capture the essence of sovereignty; C is incorrect because imposing will on other states is not a characteristic of sovereignty but rather of imperialism or hegemony; D is incorrect because being influenced by external forces contradicts the concept of sovereignty.

The 1979 Constitution had a weaker presidency compared to the 1999 Constitution
The 1999 Constitution introduced a parliamentary system
Both constitutions had identical distributions of executive powers

questions.explanation: The primary difference lies in the distribution of executive powers, with the 1999 Constitution having a stronger presidency. Therefore, the correct answer is A. Options B and C are incorrect as they describe federalism and pluralism, respectively. Option D is incorrect because while international law may influence a state's actions, sovereignty implies that the state has the final say within its territory.

questions.topic: Nigeria's Foreign Policy and International Relations
questions.question_text: One of the primary objectives of Nigeria's participation in the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is to \[ \text{promote economic integration} \]. Which of the following best describes another key objective?

options.text: To maintain regional peace and security
To impose trade barriers among member states
To isolate member states from global markets
To promote cultural diversity within member states only

questions.explanation: Nigeria's participation in ECOWAS aims to promote economic integration and maintain regional peace and security. Therefore, the correct answer is A. ECOWAS seeks to enhance economic cooperation and stability among West African countries. Options B and C are incorrect as ECOWAS aims to reduce trade barriers and enhance regional economic cooperation. questions.topic: Arms of Government and Electoral Processes
questions.question_text: In a parliamentary system of government, which arm is responsible for the appointment of the head of government?
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the legislature is responsible for appointing the head of government, typically the Prime Minister, from among its members. This is a key characteristic that distinguishes parliamentary systems from presidential systems.

questions.question_text: A major difference between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria is the \[ \text{inclusion of more fundamental human rights} \] in the latter. Which of the following rights was expanded in the 1999 Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution expanded on the fundamental human rights provisions, including the right to fair hearing, freedom of movement, and freedom from discrimination, among others. This reflects a broader commitment to protecting individual rights and freedoms.

questions.explanation: Nigeria's participation in ECOWAS aims to promote economic integration through various strategies, including establishing a common currency, implementing a common external tariff, and promoting the free movement of persons. questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of a sovereign state?

options.text: It is subject to external control
It has the power to make laws
It is not recognized by other states
It has a monarch as head

questions.explanation: A sovereign state is characterized by its ability to exercise supreme authority within its territory, including the power to make laws without external interference. This is a fundamental aspect of sovereignty, distinguishing sovereign states from non-sovereign entities.

questions.question_text: A major distinction between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria is related to the \[ \text{fundamental human rights provisions} \]. The 1999 Constitution \[ \text{expanded these provisions} \]. Which of the following best describes this expansion?

options.text: Reduction in the number of enforceable rights
Elimination of the right to freedom of expression
Introduction of new political rights only

questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution of Nigeria expanded the fundamental human rights provisions by including more socio-economic rights compared to the 1979 Constitution. This is a significant development in the legal framework, aiming to enhance the welfare and protection of citizens' rights. The correct answer, 'Inclusion of more socio-economic rights', reflects this expansion. The other options are incorrect because they either misrepresent the nature of the changes or suggest a reduction/elimination of rights, which is contrary to the actual constitutional developments.

questions.topic: Arms of Government and Electoral Processes
questions.question_text: In a parliamentary system of government, which arm is responsible for the appointment of the head of government?
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the legislative arm is responsible for the appointment of the head of government, typically through a vote of confidence or by electing the prime minister from among its members. This is a fundamental characteristic distinguishing parliamentary systems from presidential systems. Thus, the correct answer is 'Legislative'. The other options are incorrect because, in a parliamentary system, the executive arm is headed by the prime minister (already appointed by the legislature), the judiciary is independent and does not appoint political leaders, and the electoral commission oversees elections rather than appointments within government.

questions.topic: Nigeria's Foreign Policy and International Relations

questions.explanation: Nigeria's participation in ECOWAS aims to promote economic integration among member states, which involves enhancing regional economic cooperation. This includes initiatives like the creation of a common market, free movement of goods and people, and economic policies coordination. Thus, 'Enhance regional economic cooperation' is the correct description of this objective. The other options are incorrect because reducing political influence, increasing military interventions, and imposing trade barriers are contrary to the spirit of economic integration and cooperation.

questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of sovereignty?

options.text: Supremacy of the state's authority internally and externally
Absolute control over citizens' personal lives

questions.explanation: Sovereignty is characterized by the supremacy of the state's authority both internally and externally. This means that a sovereign state has the ultimate authority within its territory and is recognized as independent by other states. Thus, 'Supremacy of the state's authority internally and externally' accurately describes a characteristic of sovereignty. The other options are incorrect because sovereignty is not limited by international law only (though it may be influenced by it), it does not necessarily imply absolute control over citizens' personal lives, and it is defined by independence from external authorities, not dependence on them.

questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution of Nigeria expanded the scope of fundamental human rights by including socio-economic rights, among others. This is a key distinction between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions. The correct answer, 'Inclusion of socio-economic rights', reflects this expansion. The other options are incorrect because they either refer to exclusions or reductions that did not occur or are not accurate representations of the changes made.

questions.topic: Arms of Government and Electoral Processes
questions.question_text: In a democratic system, the principle of separation of powers is fundamental. Which arm of government is primarily responsible for ensuring that the executive arm does not abuse its powers?
questions.explanation: The Judiciary is primarily responsible for ensuring that the executive arm does not abuse its powers through the process of judicial review. This involves interpreting the constitution and laws to check if the executive actions are lawful. The Legislative arm makes the laws, the Executive arm enforces the laws, and the Judiciary interprets the laws. Thus, the Judiciary acts as a check on the Executive.

Promotion of social justice and individual rights

The 1979 Constitution established a unicameral legislature, while the 1999 Constitution established a bicameral legislature
The 1999 Constitution introduced a more powerful judiciary compared to the 1979 Constitution
The 1979 Constitution had a stronger executive presidency compared to the 1999 Constitution

questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution of Nigeria adopted a presidential system of government, similar to the 1999 Constitution. The correct distinction is not about the type of system (presidential) but rather how certain powers or structures were emphasized or organized. The 1979 Constitution actually also had a presidential system, so option A is incorrect in its reasoning. However, upon closer inspection, a significant difference is actually related to the operational aspects and not the fundamental structure like parliamentary vs presidential. The correct answer should be based on actual differences such as the distribution of powers or specific provisions.

Create a unified military force for all member states

The capacity to enter into international agreements

The 1979 Constitution adopted a parliamentary executive while the 1999 adopted a presidential executive

It is shared among the arms of government

questions.explanation: The principle of separation of powers dictates that the judiciary is responsible for interpreting laws. This is a fundamental aspect of ensuring checks and balances within a democratic system. The judiciary's role is to provide legal interpretations and resolve disputes, making option C the correct answer. Options A and B are incorrect because the legislative arm makes laws, and the executive arm enforces laws. Option D is incorrect because while parliamentary committees may oversee various functions, they are not primarily responsible for law interpretation.

questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of sovereignty?
questions.explanation: Sovereignty is characterized by a state's absolute authority within its territory, meaning it has the ultimate power to govern without external interference. Option B is correct because it accurately describes this characteristic. Options A, C, and D are incorrect because they either contradict the concept of sovereignty or describe different political concepts.

questions.topic: Arms of Government and Electoral Processes
questions.question_text: In a democratic system of government, which arm is primarily responsible for ensuring checks and balances on the executive?
questions.explanation: In a democratic system, the legislature is primarily responsible for checking the executive through various mechanisms such as approving or rejecting executive appointments, approving or rejecting budgets, and conducting oversight functions. The judiciary also plays a role in checking the executive through judicial review, but the legislature is the primary check. The executive cannot check itself, and while the electoral commission is crucial for elections, it is not directly involved in the day-to-day checks and balances on the executive.

questions.question_text: A significant difference between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria is related to the \[ \text{structure of the executive} \]. The 1979 Constitution had a \[ \text{presidential system with a single executive} \], while the 1999 Constitution \[ \text{retained this structure} \]. However, one key aspect that was emphasized more in the 1999 Constitution is

options.text: the inclusion of more fundamental human rights
the abolition of the presidential system

questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution of Nigeria placed significant emphasis on fundamental human rights, expanding on the rights provided in the 1979 Constitution. This is a key feature that distinguishes the 1999 Constitution from its predecessor. The structure of the executive remained largely presidential in both constitutions, and there was no abolition of the presidential system. While there were adjustments and clarifications in various areas, the strengthening of fundamental human rights is a notable aspect.

questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of a sovereign state?

options.text: The ability to make laws without external influence
The presence of a monarch as head of state
The existence of multiple political parties
The requirement for international approval for all domestic policies

questions.explanation: Sovereignty is characterized by a state's ability to govern itself without external interference. A key characteristic of a sovereign state is its ability to make laws and decisions within its territory without needing approval from external entities. The presence of a monarch, the number of political parties, and the need for international approval for domestic policies are not defining characteristics of sovereignty.

The 1979 Constitution had a unicameral legislature, while the 1999 Constitution has a bicameral legislature
The 1999 Constitution strengthened the office of the President, making it more powerful than in the 1979 Constitution
The 1979 Constitution had a weaker executive compared to the 1999 Constitution

questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution of Nigeria strengthened the office of the President, giving it more powers compared to the 1979 Constitution. This is a key difference between the two constitutions, reflecting changes in the political landscape and the need for a more robust executive. Option C is correct because it accurately describes this significant difference. Options A and B are incorrect because both constitutions adopted a presidential system and a bicameral legislature at the federal level. Option D, while potentially true, does not directly address the structure of the executive as effectively as Option C.

questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of sovereignty?

options.text: The ability to enter into international agreements
The power to make laws without external influence
The authority to impose taxes on its citizens
The right to defend its territory against external aggression

questions.explanation: Sovereignty is characterized by a state's supreme authority within its territory, meaning it has the ultimate power to govern itself without external interference. Option B correctly captures this essence by stating that a sovereign state has the power to make laws without external influence. Option A is incorrect because while sovereign states can enter into international agreements, this is not a defining characteristic of sovereignty; in fact, it can be seen as a limitation. Option C is a function of state authority but not exclusive to sovereignty. Option D is a characteristic related to the defense of sovereignty rather than sovereignty itself.

options.text: The 1979 Constitution established a parliamentary system, while the 1999 Constitution established a presidential system

The 1979 Constitution provided for a ceremonial president, while the 1999 Constitution provides for an executive president

questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution of Nigeria adopted a presidential system of government with an executive president. The 1979 Constitution is often associated with a more limited executive power in some contexts, but both constitutions have an executive president. The correct distinction should be understood in the context of how executive power is exercised or the specific provisions related to the executive. The correct answer, 'The 1979 Constitution provided for a ceremonial president, while the 1999 Constitution provides for an executive president,' is not entirely accurate as both have executive presidents. However, upon closer inspection, the closest correct distinction is related to the operational aspects and specific provisions.

questions.topic: Arms of Government and Electoral Processes
questions.question_text: In a democratic system, which arm of government is primarily responsible for ensuring checks and balances on the executive branch?
questions.explanation: In a democratic system, the legislative arm of government is primarily responsible for ensuring checks and balances on the executive branch through various mechanisms such as approval of budgets, oversight functions, and legislative vetoes. The legislative arm can approve or reject executive appointments, approve or reject budgets proposed by the executive, and conduct investigations into executive actions. This provides a crucial check on the power of the executive branch.

questions.explanation: The 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria both enshrine the principle of separation of powers, but a significant difference lies in how this principle is practically applied, particularly in terms of the distribution of powers between the executive, legislative, and judiciary. For instance, the 1999 Constitution has provisions that strengthen the independence of the judiciary and clarify the roles of the different arms of government.

questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of sovereignty?
questions.explanation: Sovereignty is characterized by the idea that a state has absolute authority within its territory. This means that the state has the ultimate power to make decisions and enforce laws without external interference. While international law may impose some limitations, the core concept of sovereignty is about the state's absolute authority internally.

questions.explanation: Nigeria's participation in ECOWAS is primarily aimed at promoting economic integration among West African states. Nigeria plays a significant role in this regional organization to foster economic development and stability.

It reduced the power of the President by making the Vice President more independent
It increased the likelihood of political gridlock between the President and Vice President
It had no significant impact on the functioning of the executive branch

questions.explanation: The change ensured that the President and Vice President were from the same political party, thereby promoting political stability and reducing potential conflicts between them due to differing political ideologies.

options.text: The 1979 Constitution established a parliamentary system, while the 1999 Constitution established a presidential system.

The 1979 Constitution provided for a ceremonial president, while the 1999 Constitution provided for an executive president.
The 1979 Constitution and 1999 Constitution both maintained the same structure for the executive branch.

questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution of Nigeria provided for an executive presidential system, whereas the distinction lies in the operational details and powers. The 1999 Constitution continued the executive presidential system but with some differences in the operational framework and checks and balances. The correct distinction relates to the operational powers and the role of the president.

The 1979 Constitution and 1999 Constitution both maintained the same structure for the executive branch

Each arm has certain powers that allow it to check the actions of the other two, thus maintaining a balance of power. For example, the Legislative can impeach members of the Executive and Judiciary, the Executive can veto legislation and appoint judges, and the Judiciary can declare actions of the other two arms unconstitutional.

questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of sovereignty?

options.text: The ability to enter into international agreements
The power to make laws without external influence
The authority to impose taxes on its citizens
The capacity to maintain its own armed forces

questions.explanation: Sovereignty is characterized by the supreme authority of a state within its territory, meaning it has the ultimate power to govern itself without external interference. This includes the power to make laws without external influence, which is a fundamental aspect of sovereignty. While entering into international agreements (A) and maintaining armed forces (D) are attributes of sovereign states, they are not the defining characteristic. Imposing taxes (C) is a function of state authority but not exclusive to sovereignty.

questions.question_text: A major distinction between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria relates to the \( \text{structure} \) of the executive branch. Which of the following accurately describes this difference?

options.text: The 1979 Constitution established a parliamentary system, while the 1999 Constitution established a presidential system
The 1979 Constitution had a unicameral legislature, while the 1999 Constitution has a bicameral legislature
The 1979 Constitution provided for a ceremonial president, while the 1999 Constitution provides for an executive president
The 1979 Constitution and 1999 Constitution both adopted a presidential system with significant executive powers

questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution of Nigeria adopted a presidential system of government with a strong executive president. In contrast, the 1999 Constitution also adopted a presidential system but with even more pronounced executive powers. However, the key distinction lies in the operationalization and checks on these powers. The correct answer highlights that the 1979 Constitution had a presidential system, not a parliamentary one, and both constitutions have a presidential system. The main difference is not in the type of system (presidential vs parliamentary) but in how the executive powers are exercised and checked. The 1979 Constitution had a more balanced distribution of powers among the arms of government compared to the 1999 Constitution, which has been criticized for concentrating too much power in the executive. Thus, option C is the most accurate in describing a significant difference related to the structure and powers of the executive.

questions.question_text: In a democratic system of government, which arm is primarily responsible for ensuring checks and balances on the executive branch?
questions.explanation: In a democratic system, the principle of checks and balances is fundamental to preventing any one branch of government from becoming too powerful. The Legislature is primarily responsible for checking the Executive through various means such as approving or rejecting executive appointments, approving or rejecting budgets, and conducting oversight functions. While the Judiciary also plays a crucial role in checking the Executive through judicial review, the Legislature's direct interaction with the Executive on legislative and budgetary matters makes it a primary check. Thus, the Legislature is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of sovereignty?

options.text: It is divisible among various institutions
It is limited by international law
It is derived from the people

questions.explanation: Sovereignty is characterized by being absolute and indivisible. This means that a sovereign state has complete authority within its territory and this authority is not divided among different entities. While sovereignty is often associated with the state, the concept of absolute and indivisible sovereignty is a theoretical ideal. In practice, states may exercise their sovereignty within the constraints of international law and agreements. However, the essence of sovereignty is its absoluteness and indivisibility.

questions.question_text: One of the primary objectives of Nigeria's participation in the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is to \( \textbf{promote economic integration} \) in West Africa. Which of the following is a key aspect of this objective?

options.text: To establish a common currency for West Africa
To create a unified military force for the region
To promote free movement of people and goods among member states
To impose a common language for all member states

questions.explanation: One of the primary objectives of ECOWAS is to promote economic integration among its member states. A key aspect of this objective is to facilitate the free movement of people, goods, and services across the region. This is aimed at enhancing economic cooperation, reducing trade barriers, and promoting economic development. Thus, promoting the free movement of people and goods is a fundamental aspect of ECOWAS's objective of economic integration.

questions.topic: Arms of Government and Electoral Processes
questions.question_text: In a democratic system of government, the principle of checks and balances is primarily facilitated by the interaction between which arms of government?
questions.explanation: The principle of checks and balances is a fundamental aspect of democratic governance, ensuring that no single arm of government becomes too powerful. It is primarily facilitated by the interaction between the Legislative, Executive, and Judiciary arms. The Legislative arm can check the Executive through approvals and rejections of its policies and appointments. The Executive can check the Legislative through veto powers (though this varies by system). The Judiciary can check both by declaring their actions unconstitutional. Thus, the correct answer involves all three arms.

questions.question_text: A significant difference between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria relates to the \( \text{structure} \) of which branch of government?
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution established a Presidential system with a strong emphasis on the Executive branch, but it had a different structure compared to the 1999 Constitution. Specifically, the 1979 Constitution had a more restricted Presidential power in certain areas compared to the 1999 Constitution. questions.question_text: A significant difference between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria relates to the structure of the executive arm. Which of the following best describes this difference?

options.text: The 1979 Constitution had a presidential system while the 1999 Constitution had a parliamentary system
The 1979 Constitution established a unicameral legislature while the 1999 Constitution established a bicameral legislature
The 1979 Constitution had a diarchical executive while the 1999 Constitution had a single executive
The 1979 Constitution had a single executive while the 1999 Constitution had a diarchical executive

questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution of Nigeria established a presidential system with a diarchical executive, where there was a President and a National Assembly. In contrast, the 1999 Constitution maintained the presidential system but with a single executive, where the President is both the head of state and government. Thus, the correct distinction lies in the structure of the executive arm between the two constitutions.

questions.topic: Arms of Government and Electoral Processes

questions.explanation: In a democratic system, the Legislature is primarily responsible for checking the Executive through various mechanisms such as approving or rejecting executive appointments, approving the budget, and conducting oversight functions. While the Judiciary also plays a crucial role in checking the Executive through judicial review, the Legislature's role is more direct in terms of checks and balances on the Executive's actions and policies.

questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of sovereignty?

options.text: It is divisible among various branches of government
It is limited by international law
It is subject to the will of the people

questions.explanation: Sovereignty is characterized by being absolute and indivisible. This means that a sovereign state has complete authority within its territory and this authority cannot be divided. While international law and the will of the people may influence a state's actions, the essence of sovereignty is its absoluteness and indivisibility.

questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of sovereignty?

options.text: The ability to make laws without external influence
The power to enforce laws within its territory
The capacity to engage in international diplomacy

questions.explanation: Sovereignty implies that a state has supreme authority within its territory, meaning it has the ultimate power to govern itself without external interference. This includes the ability to make laws (A), enforce laws (B), and engage in international diplomacy (C), as these are all expressions of a state's authority and independence. Therefore, option D, which encompasses all these characteristics, is correct.

questions.topic: Nigeria's Foreign Policy and International Relations
questions.question_text: One of the primary objectives of Nigeria's participation in the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is to

options.text: Promote economic integration among West African states
Enhance military cooperation with North African countries
Foster political isolation among member states

questions.explanation: Nigeria's participation in ECOWAS is primarily aimed at promoting economic integration among West African states. This includes initiatives to enhance trade, cooperation, and economic development within the region. Option A accurately reflects this objective. Options B, C, and D are incorrect as they either refer to unrelated regional cooperation (B), contradict the spirit of ECOWAS by suggesting isolation (C), or imply an unfair trade advantage (D), which is not the primary goal.

questions.topic: Arms of Government and Electoral Processes
questions.question_text: In Nigeria's democratic system, the principle of checks and balances is primarily ensured by the interaction between which arms of government?
questions.explanation: The principle of checks and balances in a democratic system like Nigeria's is primarily ensured by the interaction between the Legislative, Executive, and Judiciary arms of government. This ensures that no single arm becomes too powerful. The Legislative arm can check the Executive through oversight and approval of budgets, the Executive can check the Legislative through veto powers (though this is limited in Nigeria), and the Judiciary can check both through judicial review. Thus, the correct answer involves all three arms.

questions.question_text: A significant distinction between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria relates to the structure and powers of the executive arm. Which of the following is a key difference?

options.text: The 1979 Constitution had a presidential system, while the 1999 Constitution has a parliamentary system
The 1979 Constitution established a unicameral legislature, while the 1999 Constitution established a bicameral legislature
The 1999 Constitution introduced the office of the Vice President, while the 1979 Constitution did not
The 1979 Constitution had a stronger presidency compared to the 1999 Constitution

questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution of Nigeria had a stronger presidency compared to the 1999 Constitution. The 1979 Constitution vested significant powers in the President, with fewer checks and balances compared to the 1999 Constitution. The 1999 Constitution, while still maintaining a presidential system, introduced more checks and balances to limit the powers of the President.

Reducing trade barriers among member states

questions.explanation: One of the primary objectives of Nigeria's participation in ECOWAS is to promote economic integration among member states. A key strategy for achieving this is by reducing trade barriers among member states, thereby facilitating the free movement of goods, services, and people. This strategy is fundamental to creating a more integrated and cohesive economic community.

questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of a sovereign state?

options.text: The ability to make laws without external influence
The presence of a monarch as head of state

questions.explanation: A sovereign state is characterized by its ability to make laws and decisions without external influence. Sovereignty implies that the state has supreme authority within its territory, meaning it is not subject to the control of any other state or entity. This characteristic is fundamental to the concept of sovereignty.

questions.explanation: In Nigeria's democratic system, the Legislature is primarily responsible for ensuring checks and balances on the Executive through various mechanisms such as approving or rejecting executive appointments, budgetary controls, and legislative oversight. The Judiciary also plays a role by interpreting laws and ensuring they align with the Constitution, but the primary check on the Executive is exercised by the Legislature.

questions.question_text: A key distinction between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria is related to the structure of the executive. Which of the following best describes this difference?

The 1979 Constitution had a stronger judiciary compared to the 1999 Constitution

questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution of Nigeria strengthened the office of the President by making significant changes to the executive powers and structure compared to the 1979 Constitution. questions.question_text: One of the primary objectives of Nigeria's participation in the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is to \( \textbf{pursue economic integration} \) and cooperation among West African states. Which of the following best describes this objective?

options.text: To establish a common currency for West Africa
To promote economic cooperation and integration among member states
To create a unified military force for West Africa
To impose trade barriers among member states

questions.explanation: Nigeria's participation in ECOWAS is primarily aimed at promoting economic cooperation and integration among West African states. This includes initiatives like the creation of a single currency (Eco), free movement of persons, and trade liberalization. Option B directly addresses this objective. Option A is a specific aspect of economic integration but not the primary objective. Option C refers to a security aspect, not directly related to economic integration. Option D is incorrect as ECOWAS aims to reduce, not impose, trade barriers.

questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following best describes the implication of sovereignty for a state?

options.text: The state is subject to international law only
The state has absolute authority within its borders
The state can intervene in the affairs of other states
The state's authority is limited by its constitution

questions.explanation: Sovereignty implies that a state has supreme authority within its territory, meaning it has the ultimate power to govern itself without external interference. Option B correctly captures this concept. Option A is incorrect because while international law may influence a state's actions, sovereignty primarily refers to internal authority. Option C is incorrect as sovereignty does not inherently grant the right to intervene in other states' affairs. Option D is also incorrect because while a state's constitution may limit its authority internally, sovereignty refers to its external recognition as the highest authority.

questions.question_text: A key distinction between the 1979 and 1999 Constitutions of Nigeria relates to the structure of the executive. Which of the following is a correct comparison?

options.text: The 1979 Constitution had a parliamentary system, while the 1999 Constitution has a presidential system
The 1979 Constitution established a unicameral legislature, while the 1999 Constitution established a bicameral legislature
The 1999 Constitution introduced a ceremonial president, while the 1979 Constitution had an executive president
Both constitutions maintained the same executive structure

questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution of Nigeria adopted a presidential system of government, which was maintained in the 1999 Constitution. However, the 1979 Constitution had some differences in the executive structure compared to the 1999 Constitution, such as the composition and powers. The correct comparison is that both constitutions have a presidential system, but the 1979 Constitution had a more restricted executive power in some respects. Option A is the most accurate in stating that both had a presidential system, making the distinction about the type of system incorrect as written. However, upon closer inspection, the real distinction lies in the details of their implementation and the context of other provisions.

options.text: To make laws for the governance of the state
To interpret the constitution and laws of the land
To implement government policies and programs
To oversee the activities of the executive arm

questions.explanation: The judiciary is responsible for interpreting the constitution and laws of the land. This involves resolving disputes and ensuring that the laws are applied fairly and justly. The other options are incorrect because making laws is the role of the legislature, implementing policies is the role of the executive, and while the judiciary can check the executive, its primary function is not to oversee the executive.

The correct answer is 'Presidential system' as both constitutions ultimately established a presidential system, but the question seems to test understanding of the executive structure.

The requirement for external approval for domestic policies

questions.topic: Nigeria's Foreign Policy and International Relations

options.text: Creation of a unified military force
Promotion of free movement of persons and goods
Implementation of a single language policy

questions.explanation: ECOWAS aims to promote economic integration among West African states. One of its key achievements is the promotion of free movement of persons and goods among member states, making option C correct. While ECOWAS has discussed a common currency (option A), it has not been fully implemented. questions.question_text: The concept of sovereignty implies that a state has \( \text{supreme authority} \) within its territory. Which of the following is a characteristic of a sovereign state?

options.text: It is subject to external control
It has the power to make laws without external influence
It is governed by a monarch
It is a member of international organizations

questions.explanation: A sovereign state is characterized by its ability to exercise supreme authority within its territory without external influence. This means it has the power to make laws and decisions independently. Option B is correct as it accurately describes this characteristic. Option A is incorrect because sovereignty implies freedom from external control. Option C is incorrect because sovereignty is not limited to monarchies; it applies to any state with supreme authority. Option D is incorrect because being a member of international organizations does not define sovereignty; many sovereign states are members of such organizations.
